doc.title: Rebecca Kilgore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Hal Smith and working as co-leader
summary: A drummer praises her as co-leader; she identifies Hal Smith, whom she met in Portland in the early 80s, and they record together.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You got pretty high praise from a drummer that I know that you know very well, and he said that working with you is like having another musician in the band and a co-leader, and that he depends on you a lot because he’s stuck behind the drums, that he communicates through you. And he was telling me about some signals you make that —
That would be Hal Smith I imagine.

Yeah we’ve known each other for a long time although we haven’t worked together solidly. I first worked with him in the early ‘80s in Portland, Oregon. He was in a band I was in. And then he moved away and we kind of kept in contact. And over the last few years we’ve gotten together at a lot of Dixieland festivals and parties like this, and we do kind of classic swing material. And I guess we’ve recorded a lot and I’ve written out some arrangements for him, some basic charts. So I guess it is a cooperative venture. We both like old, weird music, so we’re in good company.
